title: Choose the visual world
question: Choose the system that should make private daily tracking feel precise, durable, and calm—or steer a fresh hand.

options.label: Utility Reading Sheet
options.lineage: municipal meter books, calibration plates, and route sheets
options.thesis: The day reads like a trusted household meter: exact inputs become a durable, inspectable record.
options.viewport: A one-handed mobile route sheet: date rail above, a broad horizontal calorie reading, paired food and water channels, and the next logging action docked at thumb height.
options.risk: Can feel bureaucratic if the readings lose warmth and breathing room.

raised.raise: Every entry gains an exact place in the day’s vertical time score.
Current state is unmistakable; active readings carry the only illuminated accent.
Dense and quiet regions alternate so the log never becomes one flat stack.

options.label: Market Receipt Ledger
options.lineage: grocery till receipts, produce scales, and handwritten household ledgers
options.thesis: Each food is a line item in a private daily receipt whose totals remain traceable.
options.viewport: A continuous receipt sheet with the day’s running total printed large, food lines grouped by time, and water clipped beside it as a narrow tally strip.
options.risk: The familiar receipt metaphor can overemphasize accounting if portions and goals feel secondary.

options.label: Action-Only Consumer Surface
options.lineage: warm consumer app surfaces with one action-only accent
options.thesis: One comfortable card per decision, with color appearing only where the user can act.
options.viewport: A friendly single column with calorie summary, swipeable nutrient groups, food log, water log, and a persistent thumb bar.
options.case: It matches iPhone habits and product clarity, but identifies less strongly with the product’s durable Nutrition Snapshot mechanism.
options.risk: Without rigorous content hierarchy it becomes indistinguishable from other wellness apps.

options.label: Deployable Daily Sheet
options.thesis: The day opens from a compact totals packet into linked nutrition, food, and water cells.
options.viewport: A compact daily packet opens in stepped sections: total first, nutrient cells second, event detail last, with no loss of context.
options.case: It expresses snapshots and progressive disclosure beautifully, but the fold grammar adds a learning cost to frequent logging.
options.risk: The parallelogram system can fight familiar form and edit affordances on a narrow phone.

options.label: Nutrition Time Score
options.thesis: Food and water events rise through a bilateral day score, with block length encoding amount.
options.viewport: A central day staff with food on one side, water on the other, and goals fixed at the top edge.
options.case: The time-order map is strong, but the notation asks the user to learn symbols before the tracker feels immediate.
options.kept: Exact temporal placement instead of an arbitrary card pile.
options.risk: Novel notation could obscure names, quantities, and editing.

options.label: Daily Step Row
options.thesis: Every eating and drinking event lights a step in a day the user composed.
options.viewport: A sixteen-step time row sits above compact channel strips for calories, nutrients, food, and water.
options.case: State and rhythm are legible, but performance-instrument energy conflicts with a neutral non-gamified tracker.
options.kept: Action color is reserved for current state and press feedback.
options.risk: Can make ordinary intake feel like a score to optimize.

options.label: Glyph Density Log
options.thesis: Nutrient density becomes literal glyph density inside one strict text grid.
options.viewport: The selected day fills one character grid, with totals as denser fields and entries as readable rows.
options.case: It is compact, but neither nutrition nor iPhone logging belongs naturally to a terminal world.
options.kept: The whole screen obeys one disciplined grid rather than mixed component styles.
options.risk: Small type and encoded density undermine accessibility.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.thesis: Daily totals are cut into inspectable blocks whose missing values reveal clear blue voids.
options.viewport: Large summary blocks create quiet gaps before smaller food and water strata continue below.
options.case: The incomplete-state metaphor is memorable, but it reduces operational clarity and would require image-heavy rendering the product does not need.
options.kept: Dense summary and quiet event regions should alternate at page scale.
options.risk: Visual spectacle can eclipse exact quantities and editing.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished neutral wellness dashboard with progress rings, stacked white cards, and a bottom tab bar.
canonCard.viewport: Greeting and date above calorie rings, nutrient cards, recent foods, water shortcuts, and persistent tabs.
canonCard.risk: Immediately familiar but intentionally indistinguishable from neighboring tracking products.
